cards.explanation: The answer is False. The elder says the truth “…abides in us and will be with us forever…” He doesn't say it stays for a season. It stays, and it stays for good, friends. I'll take a promise like that over a coupon with an expiration date any day. (2 John 1:2)

The answer is Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father. The elder says grace, mercy and peace come “…from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father…” He puts the Father and the Son together in one breath, friends. It's right there in the verse. (2 John 1:3)

The answer is walking in the truth. The elder was overjoyed to find some of the lady's children “…walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us.” Walking means living it out step by step, friends, not just nodding along. I think that news made him feel ten feet tall. (2 John 1:4)

The answer is that we love one another. The elder urges the dear lady that “…we love one another.” It's short and simple, friends, and it's not easy at all. Anybody who's shared a kitchen knows that. (2 John 1:5)

The answer is False. The elder says he's urging them “…not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning…” It's an old commandment, friends, not a fresh one. Good things don't need a new label. (2 John 1:5)

The answer is True. The elder says, “And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments.” So love isn't only a warm feeling here, friends. It shows up in how we walk. Feelings are nice, but I'd say walking is where the love gets its shoes on. (2 John 1:6)

The answer is the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. The elder says these deceivers are “…refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh.” That's the very thing they won't say, friends. He takes it seriously, so we do too. (2 John 1:7)

The answer is rewarded. The elder says, “Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.” He doesn't want what we have worked for to be lost, friends. He wants them to be fully rewarded. (2 John 1:8)

The answer is False. The elder says, “Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son.” Both, he says, so the verse doesn't leave out the Son, friends. That's what makes remaining in His teaching worth it. (2 John 1:9)

The answer is not to welcome him in or even greet him. The elder says, “…do not receive him into your home or even greet him.” This is about someone who comes without the teaching of Christ, friends. The elder is plain about it. (2 John 1:10)
The answer is True. The elder says, “Whoever greets such a person shares in his evil deeds.” He's serious about it, friends. It's a short line, and it covers a lot. (2 John 1:11)

The answer is to come and speak with them face to face. The elder writes, “…I hope to come and speak with you face to face…” He'd rather talk in person than use paper and ink, friends. I think I get that. Some things land better when you can see the other person's smile. (2 John 1:12)

The answer is joy. The elder hopes to come and speak face to face “…so that our joy may be complete.” Joy is what he wants to finish up in person, friends. I think a hug and a good talk beat any letter. (2 John 1:12)
